title: Simulation-Based Quantum Forensics for QKD: Machine Learning Attack Detection and Signature Extraction
authors: Madhab Chandra Das, Sajid Ahmed, Uzair Hussain, Van Vung Pham
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) supports secure key establishment under ideal protocol assumptions, but practical systems remain exposed to implementation-level attacks against optical channels, detectors, and controller behavior. This study presents Quantum Forensic Log (QF-LOG), a simulation-based forensic framework for analyzing aggregated QKD operational logs rather than raw quantum states. QF-LOG uses four observable features: quantum bit error rate (QBER), photon count, latency in milliseconds, and abort flag. The framework classifies normal operation and three simulated attack-related conditions: partial intercept-resend, detector-blind, and fiber-tap. A physics-inspired Generator-A dataset with 5 million balanced records was constructed using explicit mathematical generation models for all four features. A transparent threshold baseline, logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated on Generator-A. The full-feature learning models achieved macro F1-scores from 0.8211 to 0.8243 and outperformed the transparent two-feature comparator. Feature diagnostics showed that QBER contributed most, followed by latency in milliseconds and photon count, while no single feature reproduced the full feature set performance. Robustness was assessed on a separately generated Generator-B dataset of 5 million records that uses the same governing equations under shifted simulated operating parameters. Without retraining or tuning, their macro F1-scores decreased to values from 0.5645 to 0.5669. These findings show that QF-LOG can support interpretable forensic classification in a controlled synthetic setting, but stable internal evaluation does not establish reliability under changed simulated QKD operating conditions. The framework provides a documented basis for future evaluation across broader simulated settings and hardware-generated QKD logs.
summary: This paper presents QF-LOG, a simulation-based forensic framework designed to detect QKD attacks by analyzing operational log features like QBER and photon count. While the framework shows strong internal classification performance on synthetic data, the authors critically demonstrate that this performance is not robust to minor shifts in simulated operating conditions, highlighting the gap between controlled simulation and real-world reliability.
main_problem: The study addresses the need to detect and classify implementation-level attacks in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems by analyzing aggregated operational logs rather than raw quantum states.
main_result: While the forensic framework achieved high classification accuracy (up to 0.8243 F1-score) on a controlled synthetic dataset (Generator-A), performance degraded significantly (to $\approx 0.56$ F1-score) when tested on data from a slightly shifted simulation (Generator-B).
method: The authors developed the Quantum Forensic Log (QF-LOG) framework, utilizing machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, etc.) trained on four key observable features derived from QKD operational logs.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a weak coherent pulse fiber-based QKD setup. The analysis focuses on the operational logs generated by simulating various attack scenarios, including partial intercept-resend, detector-blind, and fiber-tap attacks.
key_observables: Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), photon count, latency in milliseconds, and abort flag.
important_parameters: The simulation uses parameters like mean photon number ($\mu$), fiber length ($L$), attenuation ($\alpha$), and detector efficiency ($\eta_d$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation is that the entire evaluation is based on controlled, physics-inspired synthetic data (Generator-A and Generator-B), not measurements from deployed hardware.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the system boundary showing adversarial conditions affecting observable QF-LOG features, and tables detail the parameters and performance metrics for the two distinct synthetic generators (A and B).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QF-LOG framework, details the mathematical generation of the four key features under various attack conditions using two distinct simulation generators (A and B), evaluates multiple ML models on Generator-A, analyzes feature importance, and concludes by testing model robustness on Generator-B.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the security and reliability assessment of quantum communication protocols by applying ML to system-level diagnostics, which is crucial for realizing practical quantum networks.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. System and threat model for the controlled QF-LOG simulation. The simu- lated adversarial conditions affect observable QKD operational-log features, which are analyzed through the forensic classification layer.

Figure 1 summarizes the system boundary. Alice and Bob form the QKD endpoints, while the simulated conditions affect the observable operational-log features. The resulting QF-LOG records are analyzed by the forensic classifica- tion layer to distinguish the four simulated classes. Evaluation with hardware- generated QKD logs remains future work.

Fig. 2. Row-normalized Random Forest confusion matrices for (a) the Generator-A fixed holdout evaluation and (b) the Generator-B cross-generator evaluation. Rows de- note true classes and columns denote predicted classes. N: normal; IR: partial intercept- resend; DB: detector-blind; FT: fiber-tap. Values are percentages.
